title: finding(lint): the two line-item inlineEdit advisories read only `inlineEdit: true`, so a relationship declaring 'grid' or 'form' is told to add inlineEdit, and an association declaring 'grid' or 'form' is never warned
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmSXPDB46NVRepWVrL3

Found while reviewing PR #34600 (cards #34567, #34566): L1 record 6938263188 (D2) and contract review 6938207311 (③, out-of-scope finding). Not fixed there; that PR's diff does not touch these two checks.

Suggested-grade: p2 (an authoring-time advisory gives wrong advice; no runtime effect)
Suggested-domain: `domain:objectstack` (`packages/lint/**`)

## What happens

`FieldSchema.inlineEdit` accepts `true`, `'grid'` and `'form'` (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`), and the spec's own predicate and the console's `attachInlineSubforms` treat all three as "edited inline". Two advisories in `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts` on `origin/main` 082f9c2945 read only the literal `true`:

1. Line 1090, `relationship/line-items-inline-edit`: `if (isLineItemName(obj.name) && def.inlineEdit !== true)`. A `*_line` child whose relationship already declares `inlineEdit: 'grid'` or `'form'` is still told "consider inlineEdit: true", and the fix offered (`inlineEdit: true`) would replace the author's chosen mode.
2. Line 1113, the association check: `if (def.inlineEdit === true && isAssociationName(obj.name))`. An association (comments, audit, activity) declaring `inlineEdit: 'grid'` or `'form'` clutters the parent's entry form the same way and gets no warning.

## Repro

A stack with `order` and `order_line`, where `order_line.order` is a `master_detail` with `inlineEdit: 'grid'`: `os lint` prints the line-items suggestion for it. Change the value to `true`: the suggestion disappears. An object that `isAssociationName` matches (comments, audit, activity), related to `order` with `inlineEdit: 'form'`, draws no association warning; with `true` it does. (Read from the code at the lines above; not yet run as a stack.)

## Fix direction

Both checks should ask the same question the spec predicate asks (is the relationship inline-edited at all, any of the three values), ideally by calling that predicate rather than restating it. Each rule gets a test for `'grid'` and `'form'`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `relationship/line-items-inline-edit` is silent when `inlineEdit` is `true`, `'grid'` or `'form'`.
- [ ] The association check fires for `true`, `'grid'` and `'form'`.
- [ ] Tests cover both rules for all three values.
